how_students_search: Channels. Discovery is almost entirely social and mobile. Facebook reaches about 14 million Cambodians (77.9% of the population, DataReportal Digital 2026) and Telegram about 61%, so students do not start from embassy websites; they start from the Facebook feed and Telegram channels. The three layers are: (1) the MoEYS Cambodia Facebook page (~4.2M likes) and its Telegram @moeysnews, which post every government-to-government call (Stipendium Hungaricum, CSC/China-ASEAN, GKS, MEXT co-announcement, ASEAN Scholarship, Russia, Azerbaijan, domestic 100%-tuition places) as a photo of a Khmer announcement letter; (2) large Khmer community pages and channels that repost and summarise, e.g. Scholarship for Cambodia (~167K), Ahladang (~147K), Study Abroad Center (~146K), Scholarship For Khmer (~112K), WEduShare (~233K fans plus newsletter), Cambodia Scholarship Center and Scholarar on Telegram, CamStudent (students abroad); (3) embassy pages in English (Japan, Korea, Australia Awards, US Embassy/EducationUSA, British Embassy, EU Delegation) that students reach only after a repost points them there. University international offices (RUPP IRO, ITC IRO, CADT) matter for exchange programmes and as venues (MEXT exams at IFL/RUPP, embassy info sessions) but are rarely the first touchpoint. Khmer Times is the first English summary of many MoEYS notices. Students also ask in Facebook comments, Messenger and Telegram groups, watch alumni tips on TikTok/YouTube, and walk into EducationUSA at Exchange Square Mall or into paid prep shops (Scholarar opposite RUPP, WEduAbroad, IDP) that monetise the confusion. Language and search behaviour. Students search Facebook/Telegram in Khmer with the word អាហារូបករណ៍ plus a country (អាហារូបករណ៍ជប៉ុន, អាហារូបករណ៍កូរ៉េ, អាហារូបករណ៍ចិន) or the English brand name (MEXT, GKS, CSC, Chevening); official Khmer notices use formal ministry language, while the actual application is in English (or French for Campus France, Korean forms for GKS), so many rely on a friend or a page admin to translate eligibility. What frustrates them. Reposts are screenshots that strip the link, the deadline or the year, and old calls get recirculated so students cannot tell open from closed. Deadlines are published in foreign time zones (Chevening 11:00 UTC, Australia Awards 14:00 AEST, Stipendium Hungaricum 14:00 CET, GKS KST, Fulbright US Eastern) and windows can be very short (GKS graduate embassy track ran only 12-25 Feb 2026; GKS-U 15-30 Sept) with hard-copy submission at the embassy required. Track confusion is constant: MoEYS nomination vs direct embassy vs online portal (CSC Type A embassy vs Type B university; GKS embassy vs university track; MEXT embassy vs university recommendation; Stipendium Hungaricum needs MoEYS nomination after the online form). IELTS is the biggest gate: the test costs USD 185-260 in Phnom Penh, requirements range from 6.0 (Australia Awards) to 7.0 (Fulbright) while MEXT, GKS, CSC and Stipendium Hungaricum do not require it at application, and students do not know which is which. Other pain points: 2-year/2,400-hour work-experience rule for Chevening, age caps (MEXT under 35 research, 24 undergraduate), GPA conversion from Cambodian 4.0 or Bac II grades, recommendation letters and study plans in English, transcript attestation chain university -> MoEYS -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> embassy taking 3-5 weeks because Cambodia has no apostille, and Facebook ads from agents promising guaranteed scholarships for a fee. What a page for them must do. Be Khmer-first with the English programme name kept verbatim; show every deadline converted to Phnom Penh time (ICT, UTC+7) with a countdown and an open/closed/expected-next status inferred from prior years; state in one line the level, age cap, GPA, work experience and whether IELTS is required or waived; say exactly who receives the application (MoEYS, which embassy desk, which portal) and whether hard copies are needed; link only to the official source and label reposts as unofficial; render well inside the Facebook/Telegram in-app browser on a phone and export as a shareable image card; offer filters by country, level and field; include a document checklist with the attestation timeline; and flag common scam patterns.
calendar: Annual rhythm in Phnom Penh time, based on the 2025-2026 cycles. JANUARY: Stipendium Hungaricum deadline 15 Jan (14:00 CET = 20:00 ICT) on apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu after the MoEYS call in Nov-Dec, nominations by end Feb; France Excellence (Campus France/French Embassy master's-PhD) deadline late Jan (26 Jan 2025, opened 16 Dec); many Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters deadlines (7 Jan, 15 Jan, 1 Feb are typical); CSC Type A embassy paperwork being prepared. FEBRUARY: Australia Awards intake opens 1 Feb; Chinese Government Scholarship embassy-channel deadline in the first half of Feb (8-14 Feb 2026) with online form on campuschina.org; GKS Graduate embassy track two-week window at the Korean Embassy (12-25 Feb 2026, 12 Cambodia slots); Fulbright call for the following year usually published Feb-Mar. MARCH: Chinese Government Excellence Scholarship deadline 31 Mar (23:59 Beijing); last Erasmus Mundus deadlines; Stipendium Hungaricum nominations forwarded. APRIL: Australia Awards closes 30 Apr (14:00 AEST = 11:00 ICT); Fulbright Foreign Student Program deadline 30 Apr (23:59 US Eastern), extended to 5 June in the 2027-28 cycle; ASEAN Scholarship Singapore for Cambodia opens about 1 Apr; MEXT 2027-style call announced by the Japanese Embassy and MoEYS in mid/late April. MAY: MEXT application deadline at the Japanese Embassy 22 May (2026); ASEAN Scholarship Singapore closes around 31 May; Australia Awards eligibility screening. JUNE: MEXT written exams 14 June (2026) at IFL, Royal University of Phnom Penh, interviews late June-July; Fulbright extended deadline 5 June; Australia Awards interviews; ASEAN Scholarship selection tests and interviews in Phnom Penh around June-July. JULY: MEXT embassy results; Chevening prior-cohort unconditional-offer deadline 8 July; Erasmus Mundus and EU pre-departure ceremonies; ASEAN Scholarship results. AUGUST: Chevening opens 4 Aug; MoEYS domestic 100%-tuition bachelor scholarships announced after Bac II results (10,554 places for 2026-27); Stipendium Hungaricum and Australia Awards scholars depart. SEPTEMBER: GKS Undergraduate embassy track online application 15-30 Sept (18:00 KST = 16:00 ICT) with hard copies to the Korean Embassy, 3 Cambodia slots; new Erasmus Mundus programmes begin publishing next-year deadlines; Australia Awards offers. OCTOBER: Chevening deadline 6 Oct (11:00 UTC = 18:00 ICT); EducationUSA Fair in Phnom Penh; Erasmus Mundus application portals open; Korean Embassy AKS Korean Studies track call. NOVEMBER: UWC Cambodia deadline 15 Nov; Stipendium Hungaricum 2027-28 call opens mid-Nov and MoEYS publishes the Khmer notice; Chinese Embassy publishes the next CSC notice (Nov-Dec); early Erasmus Mundus deadlines from 1 Dec. DECEMBER: France Excellence campaign opens mid-Dec; CSC online applications open; Erasmus Mundus deadlines continue; Chevening shortlisting begins with embassy interviews Feb-Mar.
